boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places with documented uses for studying, collaborating, gathering, recreation, reflection, and student activities.

cards.entity_name: Grasselli Library and Breen Learning Center
cards.title: Settle In at Grasselli
cards.subtitle: Study rooms, quiet corners, and project support under one roof
cards.notes: Reserve a group room for collaborative work, or bring an individual assignment and choose among the library’s quieter study areas.
cards.short_summary: A flexible study base with reservable rooms, research help, equipment loans, leisure collections, and spaces for focused work.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU describes Grasselli Library as containing study spaces and group meeting rooms; its student-services guide confirms that students can reserve study rooms for projects or study sessions.
cards.access_notes: Campus library rules and room-reservation requirements apply; consult the library website before visiting.

cards.title: Pair Study Time With Practical Help
cards.subtitle: A second-floor library commons connecting students with academic support
cards.notes: Use the commons as a study stop when you also need academic advising or career guidance; appointments are arranged through myJCU.
cards.short_summary: This library-based commons brings academic and career services into the same area students use for learning and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU states that the Academic Success Center and Career Center are co-located in the Mastrantoni Family Student Success Commons on the library’s second floor.
cards.access_notes: Academic Success Center appointments are made through the myJCU portal; other commons services may have separate procedures.

cards.title: Move a Group Project Into the Curiosity Lab
cards.subtitle: A named library space for innovation and collaborative student work
cards.notes: Bring an early-stage project here when your group needs a collaborative setting; confirm current availability through the library first.
cards.short_summary: A newer Grasselli Library space designed around innovation, entrepreneurship, student research, and group collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU identifies the Curiosity Lab as an innovation and entrepreneurship feature of the renovated Grasselli Library alongside new collaborative spaces for student research and group work.
cards.source_title: Alan R. Miciak, Ph.D., President of John Carroll University, Announces Plans for Retirement in May 2026
cards.access_notes: The source documents the space and its purpose but does not provide public hours or drop-in access details.

cards.entity_name: Sabo Center for Languages and Cultures
cards.title: Build a Language Project Together
cards.subtitle: Flexible workstations and presentation technology in O’Malley Center
cards.notes: Use the flexible tables for collaborative coursework, or reserve the room through CourseDog when your project needs the full space.
cards.short_summary: A technology-equipped academic workspace with 24 computers, flexible furniture, device tables, and campus printing.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU says the Sabo Center in O’Malley Center room 101 is primarily for academic work and includes 24 computer workstations, flexible furniture, a Solstice Pod, tables, and printing.
cards.access_notes: The space is reservable through CourseDog; food is prohibited because it contains educational technology.

cards.title: Screen Course Media With a Small Group
cards.subtitle: A food-friendly humanities library and theater space in O’Malley Center
cards.notes: Reserve OC 139 for a small organization event or course-related screening; plan for no more than the documented 12-person capacity.
cards.short_summary: A compact social-learning room combining a humanities collection with a theater area for coursework and organization events.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU describes the AMLC Multimedia Library in O’Malley Center room 139 as an informal social space with a humanities library and theater area, reservable by instructors and student organizations.
cards.access_notes: Reservations are handled through CourseDog; the documented safe seating capacity is 12, and the room is food-friendly.

cards.title: Use the Atrium as a Campus Crossroads
cards.subtitle: A shared student-center setting for programs, meals, and campus connections
cards.notes: Check the campus calendar before stopping in; the atrium regularly serves as a recognizable meeting and event location.
cards.short_summary: The renovated heart of the student center functions as a common gathering point beside campus services and activity spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU identifies the Lombardo Student Center Atrium as a campus event and gathering location, and the university documents that the atrium was completely renovated.
cards.access_notes: Public-event schedules do not establish unrestricted access; normal student-center policies and event setups apply.

cards.title: Join a Conversation Across Traditions
cards.subtitle: A Lombardo Student Center gathering place for interfaith programming
cards.notes: Watch the campus events calendar for an open program, then use the atrium as a setting for respectful conversation and connection.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated gathering area where JCU hosts student-led programs centered on fellowship and interreligious understanding.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU lists the Interfaith Atrium in Lombardo Student Center as the location of its Breaking Bread interfaith lunch, an event open to all students, faculty, and staff and led in part by student fellows.
cards.access_notes: Attend only during an announced open program or according to current Campus Ministry access practices.

cards.title: Gather for a Friendly Game
cards.subtitle: A Dolan Center lab used for organized gaming activities
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled student activity or authorized lab session rather than assuming open play; equipment access may be supervised.
cards.short_summary: A named campus gaming facility that supports structured, social play within the Dolan Center for Science and Technology.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU’s current campus map places the Esports Lab in the Dolan Center, and a 2025 university program report documents friendly games held there as an evening activity.
cards.source_title: John Carroll University Hosted First-Ever Summer in The Heights Pre-College Program
cards.access_notes: The source confirms programmed use, not general drop-in access; verify eligibility and scheduling before visiting.

cards.title: Take a Study Session Above the Quad
cards.subtitle: An outdoor Dolan Center study area with tables overlooking campus
cards.notes: Bring reading or a small-group assignment when weather permits, and follow any posted building or balcony access restrictions.
cards.short_summary: This elevated Dolan Center spot gives students tables for studying or talking while looking toward the Academic Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carroll News documented students using the Dolan Science Center balcony for studying and relaxing, noting its study tables and view over the Academic Quad.
cards.source_title: Perfect Study Spots on John Carroll’s Campus
cards.access_notes: Because the supporting student report predates recent campus projects, confirm current balcony access and obey posted restrictions.

cards.title: Move the Meetup Onto the Main Quad
cards.subtitle: A central lawn used for games and shared outdoor activities
cards.notes: Choose the quad for an informal daytime meetup or campus activity, while yielding to scheduled programs and field conditions.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed outdoor campus space where university programming has included group recreation and student-centered activities.
cards.evidence_claim: JCU’s 2025 Summer in The Heights report documents participants playing kickball on the Main Quad, demonstrating its use for shared outdoor recreation.
cards.source_title: John Carroll University Hosted First-Ever Summer in The Heights Pre-College Program
cards.access_notes: Outdoor availability can change with university events, maintenance, and weather; scheduled activities take priority.
